newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas off sharply as OTC players sell June.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas off sharply as OTC players sell June.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures saw active trade on Friday morning as prices fell by over 0.50 pence a therm in front month July.

July traded as low as 10.50 pence a therm as 70 lots were traded in three deals in that month. A total of 180 lots were done in seven trades, with July, August, September and December all seeing heavy losses.

A physical trader said the OTC market was weaker as several traders were looking to offload volumes of June gas. This was reported done at 10.85 pence and possibly 10.75 pence on the physical market the day after the June futures contract closed, although the trades were not confirmed.
He said that by midday the best bids on June were 10.65 pence a therm, and one or two companies were said to be watching the fall and waiting for an opportunity to buy cheap gas.

On futures July saw the biggest fall, losing 0.54 pence by the close of the session, while August traded at 10.60 pence, down 0.48 pence, and September was off by 0.43 pence at 10.80. As a result the contango between the three months has steepened.
Open interest on the June contract when it closed was 170 lots or 170,000 therms a day, which will now be physically delivered.
